title: Benefit Overpayment Accounts — Installments Counted in Arrears by Age of the Default
content:
For the arrears payment on a defaulted Benefit Overpayment Accounts repayment plan, how far the installments counted reach depends on how long ago the plan broke down, dated by its most recent returned installment: the most recent return entry booked on the overpayment. The age of the default is counted in calendar days from that return's booking date to the handling date.

| Return booked before the handling date | Installments counted |
|---|---|
| More than 60 days (the long default-age days) | Only the installments fallen due up to the return: the first installment plus one for each whole month from the first installment due date to the return's booking date |
| More than 30 days (the short default-age days) and no more than 60 days | Those installments plus one more |
| 30 days or fewer, or no installment has been returned | Every installment fallen due to the handling date: the first installment plus one for each whole month from the first installment due date to the handling date |

## Interpretation

- Exactly 60 days falls in the middle row; 61 days falls in the first row.
- Exactly 30 days falls in the last row; 31 days falls in the middle row.
- "No installment has been returned" means that the overpayment's ledger carries no return entry.

## Worked cases (hypothetical dates)

First installment due 15 January; the most recent return entry was booked on 20 March, two whole months after 15 January.

| Handling date | Days since the return | Row | Installments counted |
|---|---|---|---|
| 25 May | 66 | More than 60 | 1 plus 2, that is 3 |
| 10 May | 51 | More than 30, no more than 60 | 3 plus 1, that is 4 |
| 15 April | 26 | 30 or fewer | 1 plus 3 whole months to 15 April, that is 4 |
